texts: The village pays the Keepers in food and shelter.
The village pools its fishing harvest, grain trade, and garden produce.
Each Keeper draws a share from the pool.
The villagers use coin for trade with outside merchants.

fields.sentence: The village pays the Keepers in food and shelter.

review.notes: "the Keepers" correctly takes the capitalized-plural-label Name-only treatment (one symbol, Name atom, no GroupOf, no keeper typing). The one judgment call is Recipient for the paid party (defensible as the goal of a transfer) versus Theme as a bare direct object; the medium PP stays the surface-preposition oblique In, which the instruction set prefers over a near-fit Instrument.

fields.sentence: The village pools its fishing harvest, grain trade, and garden produce.

q2_gaps: an aggregate/collective predicate ('pool' — combine into one pool, the same family as gather/assemble) taking COORDINATED OBJECTS: the collective carve-out is stated only for a coordinated/plural SUBJECT ('one event with multiple Agent atoms'), so the distributive default applies and yields three separate pooling events rather than one aggregation of the three things
review.notes: Compound kinds fused with head genus only and the noun modifiers (fishing/grain/garden) correctly left unexposed; 'its' attaches by Possession (not PartOf) since a harvest/trade/produce is not a component of a village. Simple present correctly carries no status atom.

fields.sentence: Each Keeper draws a share from the pool.

review.notes: Explicit universal "each" correctly takes the distributing rule over (Member $x keeper) at STV 1.0 0.9 with its QuantifierPhrase companion, and the dependent indefinite "a share" is a Skolem function (sk_share $x). Capitalized "Keeper" is rightly a common-noun label with no Name atom, and "the pool" is a top-level-asserted constant filling Source.

fields.sentence: The villagers use coin for trade with outside merchants.

q1_issues.issue: The trade is reified and asserted at top level as an occurring event, though the sentence names it only as what the coin is used for, and the oblique-object rule keeps a bare noun as a constant, i.e. (For sk_use_1 trade).
(Agent sk_trade_1 sk_villagers_1) gives the villagers a role in a trading event the sentence never predicates of them.

(Inheritance outside_merchant outside) exposes an attributive-only modifier that fails the predication test ('the merchant is outside' does not mean 'from outside'), so the genus merchant should stand alone.

q2_gaps: purpose/ground 'for'-PP whose object is an eventuality noun carrying its own comitative argument ('for trade with outside merchants') - the preposition-named oblique takes a bare constant object and offers no slot for the 'with' phrase
review.notes: The definite-plural group event plus the per-member distribution rule for 'the villagers use coin' follows the grouped-plural doctrine correctly, at the right strength and confidence.

issues.reason: The oblique-object half stands — bare 'trade' is a non-specific mass/abstract noun, and the preposition-named oblique's object NP follows the ordinary NP rules ('a bare mass / domain / proper name stays a constant'), so (For sk_use_1 trade) is the licensed form and no sk_trade_1 witness may be minted; the 'asserted as an occurring event' half overstates, since the instruction set's own control / causative doctrine holds that a tenseless reified event 'asserts or denies nothing about occurrence'.

The atom is not false of the sentence's content — the villagers are the understood trading party by the same subject-control default the instruction set applies to purpose complements ('copy the controller's role in'); what is unlicensed is the reification itself, already covered by issue 0.

'outside' in 'outside merchants' is an attributive-only relational modifier — 'the merchant is outside' states a physical position the text never claims — so it fails the predication test and is never exposed as a modifier genus, exactly the 'assistant secretary' case that keeps its head genus only.

gaps_confirmed: a purpose/ground 'for'-PP whose object is an eventuality noun carrying its own comitative argument ('for trade with outside merchants'): the licensed (For <event> trade) oblique takes a bare constant object and offers no slot for the 'with' phrase, so the outside merchants cannot be carried at all
new_gaps: the implicit participant of a nominal purpose adjunct ('use coin for trade' — whose trade?) has no licensed carrier: the controller-copying rule is defined only for infinitival complements and control verbs, so a bare purpose noun cannot record its understood agent
adjudication.defect_summary: For the confirmed modifier issue the compliant form is the head genus alone — (Inheritance outside_merchant merchant) with no (Inheritance outside_merchant outside). For the standing half of issue 0 the compliant form keeps the oblique object a bare constant, (For sk_use_1 trade), dropping sk_trade_1 and both of its Agent atoms — after which 'with outside merchants' has NO licensed form at all and must be left out with the gap recorded.
adjudication.notes: The definite-plural group event plus its per-member distribution rule, and the strengths/confidences throughout, are correct. The reification was graceful improvisation reaching for the uncovered comitative, but it broke a rule that IS covered (bare oblique objects stay constants).
